# How Much Does Disney+ Cost?

Disney+ costs $12.49 a month for an ad-based subscription or $21.49 a month for an ad-free experience.

Written by

Lisa Mulka

Lisa Mulka

Contributing Writer

Tommy Tindall

Expertise

Tommy Tindall is a lead writer and content strategist covering how to make money — and how to keep it. He’s recorded and written about his experience testing popular gig jobs like driving for Uber, delivering with DoorDash and full-service shopping for Instacart. He loves making an extra buck, but laments the hours of awkward silence he endured as an Uber driver (never again).

Cool kids might call him a content creator because he makes YouTube videos for the NerdWallet channel and app, but he himself is no longer very cool. Ask him about budgeting apps — he's tried most of them, but still prefers a good ole Google sheet to track spending. Then be sure to smash that “like” and “subscribe” button.

Before NerdWallet, Tommy held decidedly more boring jobs at Fannie Mae and Booz Allen Hamilton. Today, he feels super privileged to write for you, the consumer.

Courtney Neidel

She joined NerdWallet in 2014 and spent six years writing about shopping, budgeting and money-saving strategies before being promoted to editor. Courtney has been interviewed as a retail authority by "Good Morning America," Cheddar and CBSN. Her prior experience includes freelance writing for California newspapers.

Updated Sep 24, 2026

How is this page expert verified?

NerdWallet's content is fact-checked for accuracy, timeliness and relevance. It undergoes a thorough review process involving writers and editors to ensure the information is as clear and complete as possible.

Disney’s popular streaming service offers a robust library. It ranges from classic animated films and exclusive Marvel content like the new "Wonder Man" series to hit shows like "The Simpsons." 

But just how much does Disney+ cost? It starts at $12.49 a month. 

## How much does a Disney+ subscription cost per month?

The final cost of Disney+ depends on whether you’re willing to put up with ads. 

The ad-supported plan is $12.49 a month. The ad-free Premium plan costs $21.49 a month or $214.99 a year.

That said, Disney+ offers some of the most flexible package deals of any streaming platform. Users can bundle Disney+ with other streaming services for enhanced savings and a larger content menu. Packages include:

- Disney+ (with ads) and Hulu (with ads): $12.99 a month. 
- Disney+ (with ads), Hulu (with ads) and ESPN Select (with ads): $21.99 a month. 
- Disney+ (ad-free) and Hulu (ad-free): $21.99 a month. 
- Disney+ (ad-free), Hulu (ad-free) and ESPN Select (with ads): $32.99 a month.

Some existing subscribers have the “legacy” bundle for $27.99 a month, which combines Disney+ (ad-free), Hulu (with ads) and ESPN Select (with ads). This plan is no longer available for new subscribers.

This tool was created with the assistance of AI. It has been reviewed by our editorial team for accuracy and quality.

## What does Disney+ include?

The ad-supported version of Disney+ includes:

- Disney movies and TV series.
- Star Wars and Marvel content.
- 4K playback (on select titles).
- The ability to stream up to four devices simultaneously.
- A total of seven user profiles.

In addition to ad-free streaming, the premium version also offers:

- Unlimited downloads on up to 10 devices.
- Dolby Atmos sound (on select titles).

## Does Disney+ allow password sharing?

Disney does not allow sharing of accounts or subscriptions outside of a single household, which it defines as devices that are linked to your personal primary residence.

Disney is raising prices for Disney+ and Hulu. See what the streaming services will cost. - CBS News

# Disney is raising prices for Disney+ and Hulu. See what the streaming services will cost.

 By 

 Mary Cunningham 

Mary Cunningham Reporter, MoneyWatch

 Mary Cunningham 

 September 23, 2026 / 2:59 PM EDT / CBS News 

The Walt Disney Company is raising prices for several of its subscription plans, including Disney+, Hulu and certain bundle options.

Both standalone ad-free plans for Disney+ and Hulu are increasing by $2.50, or 13%, bringing the total cost to $21.49 a month for each, the entertainment giant told CBS News on Wednesday. The cost of Disney+ and Hulu plans with ads will both rise by 50 cents to $12.49 a month. The ad-free plan that bundles the services will also go up by $2 to $21.99.

The company said it will continue pricing its most popular bundle, a joint Disney+/Hulu subscription with ads, at $12.99.

The price hikes for new subscribers take effect immediately, while existing subscribers will see the new billing rates kick in next month. Here's a full breakdown of Disney's new subscription prices:

- Disney+, Hulu Bundle (with ads) unchanged at $12.99 per month
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium (ad-free) is increasing by $2 from $19.99 to $21.99 per month
- Disney+ and Hulu standalone plans (with ads) are increasing by 50 cents from $11.99 to $12.49 per month
- Disney+ and Hulu Premium standalone plans (ad-free) are increasing by $2.50 from $18.99 to $21.49 per month
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle (with ads) is increasing by $2 from $19.99 to $21.99 per month
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle Premium (ad-free) is increasing by $3 from $29.99 to $32.99 per month
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle (with ads) unchanged at $35.99 per month
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle Premium (ad-free) unchanged at $44.99 per month

Last year, Disney announced that it would combine Disney+ and Hulu to create a "unified app experience." Hulu subscribers can now link their profiles and watch history on Disney+, CEO Josh D'Amaro said during the company's earnings call in August. 

Disney also offers bundle plans with ESPN, which it acquired in 1996 as part of its acquisition of Capital Cities/ABC.

 Edited by Alain Sherter

# Disney+ raises prices by 13% with monthly ad-free plan now over $250 a year

by Michael Gwilliam

Published: Sep 23, 2026, 16:01

Disney/Dexerto

Disney+ is getting more expensive in the US, with its ad-free Premium plan climbing to $21.49 a month, less than a year after its last price increase.

The new rate is $2.50 higher than the previous $18.99 monthly price, an increase of about 13%. Disney’s US subscription page also lists Premium at $214.99 a year, up from $189.99, while the ad-supported plan has risen 50 cents to $12.49 a month.

According to Bloomberg, the increase takes effect as early as September 23 for new subscribers. Existing monthly subscribers will see the higher price on their next bill.

## Disney+ Premium now costs over $250 a year when paid monthly

At $21.49 a month, a full year of Disney+ Premium costs $257.88 for subscribers who pay monthly. The $214.99 annual option is $42.89 cheaper, though it requires paying for the year upfront.

The increase follows Disney’s 2025 price increase, which took Premium from $15.99 to $18.99 a month and raised its annual price from $159.99 to $189.99. Compared with that earlier monthly rate, Premium now costs $5.50 more each month.

Disney

Disney+ launched in the US in 2019 at $6.99 a month. Its latest Premium price is more than three times that original rate, although the service has since added a cheaper plan with ads.

The higher bill also arrives days after Disney+’s ad-free terms drew scrutiny. Disney says Premium movies and series play without commercial interruptions, but select live and linear programming can still carry ads.

The listed prices are in US dollars and apply to US subscriptions. Prices and plans vary by country.

The Disney+ price increase applies to new subscriptions starting today, September 23, 2026. If you already have a Disney+ subscription, the new pricing will show up in your billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026.

### New Disney+ Pricing and Percentage Increases

New subscribers pay the updated prices right away. If you're a current subscriber, your rate stays the same until your next billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026. Check your account settings for your exact renewal date so you know when the new price takes effect.

# Disney+ gives a new customer nothing free: you pay $12.49 or $21.49 from the first day, a partly used term is not refunded, and the cut-off is 11:59 P.M. Eastern the day before your term ends.

Think twice before signing up expecting a trial or a welcome price. The only price break the homepage ties to a new customer is the $6.49 student bundle. Everyone else pays the plan price on day one, and the Agreement adds two clauses worth knowing: a failed payment leaves you liable for collection costs, and disputes go to individual arbitration unless you opt out within 30 days.

No trial, no bonus, no referral$12.49 or $21.49 a month Cut-off 11:59 P.M. ET Examined Sep 25

No trial and no sign-up reward of any kind, on every Disney+ page we read on September 25, 2026

The homepage lists Disney+ (With Ads) at $12.49 a month and Disney+ Premium (No Ads) at $21.49 a month or $214.99 a year, and nothing else for a new customer. The Subscriber Agreement, which carries the line “Updated: 2/5/2026”, leaves the door open and shuts it: “Availability of a free trial is not guaranteed and, if one is available, is only available on the specified terms of the free trial.” On our read date no page offered one. The one price aimed at a new customer is the student bundle: $6.49 a month for the ad-supported Disney+, Hulu Bundle while enrollment stays verified through SheerID, then $12.99.

A term you have paid for stays paid, and the clock is Eastern time. The Agreement says: “EXCEPT AS REQUIRED BY APPLICABLE LAW, WE DO NOT REFUND OR CREDIT FOR PARTIALLY USED SUBSCRIPTION TERMS AND/OR BILLING PERIODS, ALTHOUGH WE MAY PROVIDE SUCH REFUNDS OR CREDITS ON A CASE-BY-CASE BASIS IN OUR SOLE AND ABSOLUTE DISCRETION.” On the annual plan that is $214.99 paid up front. Cancel on day two and you keep Disney+ to the end of the term and get nothing back.

Disney+ has raised prices four times in four years. The latest increase takes effect September 23, 2026, pushing Disney+ Premium from $18.99 to $21.49 per month, a roughly 13% jump, according to Bloomberg and Variety. Existing monthly subscribers will see the new rate on their next billing cycle; annual plan and promotional pricing terms were not confirmed across all account types in available reporting. If you’re concerned about paying too much across your subscriptions, it may be worth a closer look at your monthly bills.

## What You’ll Pay Now

| Plan | Old Price | New Price | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disney+ Premium (ad-free) | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Hulu ad-free | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |

| Disney+ with ads | , | $12.49 | +$0.50 |

### The Bundle Math Still Works, Barely

Buying both ad-free plans separately now costs more than twice the bundle price.

Buying both standalone ad-free plans costs $42.98 per month, while the ad-free bundle comes in at $21.99, a savings of roughly $21 per month. The bundle is only $0.50 more than the price of either individual service alone, according to Bloomberg.

## Who Gets Hit and When

The new rates apply immediately to new subscribers, with existing monthly customers billed at the next cycle.

New subscribers pay the higher rate starting September 23, 2026. Existing monthly subscribers absorb the increase on their next billing cycle. Not all annual, grandfathered, and promotional pricing terms were clarified in available reporting.

### Disney+ vs. Netflix: The Gap Narrows

Disney+ Premium remains cheaper than Netflix Premium, though the margin between them continues to shrink.

At $21.49, Disney+ Premium still trails Netflix Premium’s reported $26.99 per month, according to Bloomberg. The $5.50 difference is real, though catalog depth and stream-limit policies vary between the two services.

### The Ad-Supported Tier at $12.49

For subscribers managing rising ad-free costs, Disney’s lower tier offers a clear alternative.

For subscribers managing multiple ad-free tiers, the ad-supported Disney+ plan at $12.49 per month is the most direct cost-reduction option Disney currently offers.

# Disney+ Price Hikes & Price History (2026)

Updated October 5, 2026 · Researched & fact-checked by Shaheer

Disney+ has raised the ad-free Premium plan four years running: $10.99 → $13.99 (2023) → $15.99 (2024) → $18.99 (October 2025) → $21.49 (September 23, 2026). The ad-supported tier climbed from $7.99 to $12.49 over the same period. The 2026 round was a 13% rise on Premium and 50 cents on the ad plan, and it took Disney+ past $20/month for the first time.

## At a glance

Current price

$21.49 (Premium (no Ads))

Last increase

September 23, 2026 (+13.2%)

Total change tracked

+95.5%

Tracked increases

5

## Key takeaways

- Disney+ has raised the ad-free Premium plan every year since 2023: $10.99 → $13.99 → $15.99 → $18.99 (October 2025).
- The ad-supported tier climbed from $7.99 to $11.99 over the same period.
- Disney deliberately widens the price gap to push subscribers toward the cheaper ad tier.
- The Disney+/Hulu/ESPN bundle is the main way to soften the per-service cost if you watch all three.
- Disney+ Premium is $21.49/month as of September 23, 2026 — past $20 for the first time, and the fourth increase in four years.
- The ad plan rose only 50 cents to $12.49 while ad-free rose $2.50, widening the gap to $9.00 a month.
- The ad-free Disney+/Hulu bundle at $21.99 now costs barely more than Disney+ Premium alone — 50 cents for a second service.
- Premium has risen 95% since 2023, from $10.99 to $21.49.

## Disney+ price increase history

## What Disney+ costs right now

- Basic (with Ads): $12.49 (US)

## Disney+ price history: $10.99 to $21.49 in four years

Disney+ has increased its ad-free Premium price three years running, from $10.99 in 2023 to $13.99, then $15.99, and $18.99 in October 2025. That is roughly a 73% rise in two years, one of the steepest in streaming.

The strategy is explicit: Disney widens the gap between the ad-free and ad-supported plans to nudge subscribers toward advertising, which it monetises separately. Leadership has framed ads as central to streaming profitability, so the ad-free tier absorbs most of the increases.

With Disney bundling Hulu and ESPN and changing plan structures frequently, it is easy to lose track of what you actually pay. Recording your real monthly charge is the only reliable way to catch each annual increase.

On reducing the cost, you have three realistic levers. The ad-supported tier at $11.99 is the cheapest way to keep watching. The annual Premium plan ($189.99) works out below twelve monthly payments if you stay subscribed year-round. And if you also watch Hulu or ESPN, the Disney bundle is priced below buying the services separately. Given Disney has raised the ad-free tier every year since 2023, treating another increase as likely and pre-deciding your ceiling is the sensible approach.

The September 23, 2026 round was the fourth in four years and the first to take Disney+ past $20: Premium went $18.99 to $21.49, a 13% rise, while the ad-supported plan moved just 50 cents to $12.49. Counting from 2023 the ad-free plan has gone $10.99 to $21.49 — 95%, close to a doubling in three years.

The widening gap is the whole strategy in one number. Ad-free is now $9.00 a month more than the ad tier, up from $3.00 in 2023. Disney raises the ad-free plan hard
